analogies.sourceSystem: Airport Runway Scheduling & Air Traffic Control

mappings.reason: Both arrive unpredictably and require prioritized processing.
Both are scarce physical resources serving one unit at a time.
Both assess incoming units and assign queue priority.
Both hold pending units when capacity is saturated.

brokenBridges.reason: Medical condition degrades over time if untreated, unlike delayed flights.
Treatment duration varies widely per patient compared to standard flight landing slots.

transferableSolutions: Implement predictive arrival modeling based on weather/flu season data
Create fast-track express lanes for non-critical cases to reduce queue depth
Dynamic resource pre-allocation based on incoming surge telemetry

mappings.reason: Both involve sudden medium density shifts generating pressure waves.
Both gradually displace fluid/air without acoustic shockwave build-up.

brokenBridges.reason: Biological beak deforms slightly under pressure; steel train hulls are rigid bodies.

transferableSolutions: Bio-inspired wedge nose cone geometry for high-speed transport vehicles
Varying cross-sectional taper ratios along vehicle front

mappings.reason: Both introduce phase delay into system feedback.
Both absorb transient spikes to prevent overshoot.

brokenBridges.reason: Supply chain managers panic-order under scarcity, unlike automated linear PID controllers.

transferableSolutions: Point-of-sale telemetry sharing to eliminate feedback delays
Derivative gain smoothing on automated reorder triggers

mappings.reason: Both utilize thermal buoyance stack effect for air displacement.
Both absorb daytime heat and release it during cool night periods.

brokenBridges.reason: Termites constantly seal and open pores; buildings rely on static mechanical dampers.

transferableSolutions: Nighttime thermal purging of heavy concrete building cores
Buoyancy-driven chimney ventilation shafts in high-density office towers

mappings.reason: Both act as indirect signals indicating path efficiency.
Both decay stale information so agents don't use outdated routes.

brokenBridges.reason: Too many cars following high-score route create instant traffic jams.

transferableSolutions: Stigmergic route scoring with exponential decay time-to-live
Probabilistic routing choice to prevent single-path saturation

mappings.reason: Both reduce surface contact area with liquid droplets.
Both carry surface debris away without external energy.

brokenBridges.reason: Botanical leaves regenerate wax layer; industrial glass coatings wear down over time.

transferableSolutions: Hierarchical micro-nano surface patterning for hydrophobic applications

mappings.reason: Both represent foreign entities seeking system compromise.
Both filter out normal self-behavior to flag non-self anomalies.
Both retain rapid response capabilities against known repeat threats.

brokenBridges.reason: Over-aggressive immune response destroys healthy tissue; strict cyber security can block legitimate user workflows.

transferableSolutions: Negative selection anomaly detectors for un-cataloged zero-day exploits
Quarantine sandboxing prior to full system isolation

mappings.reason: Both create channelized vortices that delay boundary-layer aerodynamic stall.
Both maintain lift forces under steep angles of attack.

brokenBridges.reason: Whale flippers move silently in water; high-speed turbine blade bumps produce tonal noise if un-tuned.

transferableSolutions: Tubercles leading edge modifications to boost low-wind power output
Vortex generators on wing leading edges for pitch stability
